content.text: You are an agent that answers a question by grounding it in the frozen training references: retrieve the closest references, follow their format and vocabulary exactly, and verify the draft answer before submitting it.

You are an expert medical diagnostician. Based on the patient's symptoms, provide a diagnosis.

Possible diagnoses include: drug reaction, allergy, chicken pox, diabetes, psoriasis, hypertension, cervical spondylosis, bronchial asthma, varicose veins, malaria, dengue, arthritis, impetigo, fungal infection, common cold, gastroesophageal reflux disease, urinary tract infection, typhoid, pneumonia, peptic ulcer disease, jaundice, migraine.

Please analyze the symptoms step by step, then provide your final diagnosis in the format:
[DIAGNOSIS]diagnosis_name[/DIAGNOSIS]

For example:
[DIAGNOSIS]diabetes[/DIAGNOSIS]


## Patient Symptoms
I have been having a lot of pain in my back and neck. I have also been coughing a lot and I feel weak. I have been dizzy and I have trouble standing up straight.

Please provide your reasoning and final diagnosis.

REFERENCE PROFILE (derived from 200 training references)
- Answer shape: 1 part in 100%; each reference answer is a single part.
- Reference labels (copy character for character; never add, remove, reorder or re-word characters, and never append a generic word the references do not use):
  allergy (10), arthritis (10), chicken pox (10), dengue (10), diabetes (10), impetigo (10), bronchial asthma (9), cervical spondylosis (9), common cold (9), drug reaction (9), fungal infection (9), gastroesophageal reflux disease (9), hypertension (9), malaria (9), peptic ulcer disease (9), pneumonia (9), psoriasis (9), typhoid (9), urinary tract infection (9), varicose veins (9), jaundice (7), migraine (7)

A: typhoid

Q: I have a lot of pain in my legs, especially when I stand for long periods of time. The skin around my veins is red and inflamed, and it is itchy. I also get regular cramps.
A: varicose veins

Q: I have a lot of burping and belching. I get chest discomfort that goes up my neck and into my jaw and arm. I have pressure and tension in my chest.
A: gastroesophageal reflux disease

[8]
Q: I've been having a lot of pain in my lower abdomen, and it feels like my bladder is about to explode when I urinate. I've also been feeling very weak and have had a low body temperature since these symptoms started.
A: urinary tract infection

Q: I have a rash on my face and near my nose. It's been there for a few days and it's starting to spread down my arms and legs.
A: impetigo

Q: I've been having migraines and headaches, and I can't sleep. My muscles are twitching and trembling, and I feel dizzy.

A: common cold

A: fungal infection

[13]
Q: My skin is dry and flaky, and I get infections easily. My joints are in a lot of pain, and the skin on my knees and elbows is peeling off.
A: psoriasis

[14]
Q: I've been feeling really grumpy and gloomy lately, and I've also noticed a change in my vision. I think it might be a migraine.
A: migraine

[15]
Q: I have to go to the bathroom a lot, but only a few drops of urine come out. I have severe stomach pains and an overwhelming urge to urinate.
A: urinary tract infection

[16]
Q: I have a fever and I feel really lightheaded and woozy. My heart is pounding and my head is really foggy. I can't think straight and everything looks blurry.
A: drug reaction

[17]
Q: I have a skin condition that causes dry, red, scaly patches on my skin. It can be itchy and painful, and it can get worse when I'm stressed or if I'm exposed to certain triggers, like sunlight or certain chemicals.
A: psoriasis

[18]
Q: I've had low temps and blood in my urine for the past three days. My pee smells terrible, and my head hurts so much. I can't control when I need to pee.
A: urinary tract infection

[19]
Q: I sometimes have blood in my urine and I feel a little sick. I also sometimes have really bad smelling pee and I get really hot at night.
A: urinary tract infection

[20]
Q: I've been having neck pain, and I've been feeling lightheaded. I've also been having trouble standing still.
A: cervical spondylosis

## How to answer

1. The reference profile and the closest training references are given above. Treat their
   answers as the authority on vocabulary, surface form and answer shape for this task.
2. If the question looks like it comes from a family of questions that recur, use
   `retrieve_examples` with a query built from the decisive details of the question to pull
   more references of that family, and `search_examples` to grep the reference set for a
   term that must appear in the answer.
3. Decide the answer from the question first, then render it the way the references render
   theirs:
   - When a reference label list is given, use its exact spelling: if your answer is the same
     thing as a listed label but differs in characters, output the listed label character for
     character. Never add, drop, reorder or re-word characters, and never append a generic
     word the references do not use. If the correct answer truly is not in the list, still
     give it, written in the same style as the listed labels.
   - Match the usual number of parts and the usual separators. Include every part that
     applies: a partial answer is scored as wrong, extra parts are scored as wrong, so be
     complete and precise.
   - Keep any markup the question asks for exactly as the question spells it.
4. Before submitting, call `check_answer` with your draft answer and fix anything it flags,
   then call `check_answer` again on the corrected draft.
5. Reply as JSON: `{"reasoning": "[your reasoning]", "final_answer": "[your answer]"}`


FINAL OUTPUT REQUIREMENT (mandatory, overrides anything else): Your final message MUST be a single JSON object with exactly two string fields, "reasoning" and "final_answer". Put the answer itself (keeping any required markup such as [DIAGNOSIS]...[/DIAGNOSIS]) inside "final_answer". Output nothing outside the JSON object.
